q: Our EU importer asks for our installation's name, address and coordinates for CBAM. Why?
title: Installation details for CBAM
short: CBAM data is tied to the installation where goods were made, not to the company. Importers must identify each installation in their declaration, so they ask for its name, address, coordinates and production route. Give details for the plant that actually made the goods.
audience: Exporters with one or several plants supplying EU importers

ul: Geographic coordinates of the main site.

p: Each plant needs its own record. Do not send one company figure for goods made at different sites.
Use the same details every time, so the importer's records match across periods.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, power and production records into dated, fingerprinted installation records, the starting point for the actual emissions your EU importer asks for.

sources.label: European Commission, CBAM legislation and guidance
